sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project name, scripts, and libraries
sections.what: Gives the project its name and version, lists four commands (dev, build, start, lint), and lists the libraries the site uses for pages, animation, icons, and styling tools.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup for a Next.js project so that a developer can start the site with one command.
sections.watch_out: Adding or removing a library here does not update the installed copy until npm install is run again.

summary: The project's ID card and shopping list: its name, the commands to run it, and the libraries it needs.
purpose: Tells npm, the package installer, which libraries to download and which commands to offer, such as starting the site or building it.
why: Every Node.js project needs this file. It lists the exact libraries the site uses so that the same setup can be rebuilt on another computer.
how: When someone runs npm install, the tool reads the dependencies and downloads them. When someone runs a script such as dev, build, start, or lint, npm runs the matching command for Next.js.
inputs: The developer's commands in a terminal, such as npm run dev or npm run build.
outputs: A local development server, a production build, or lint results. Downloaded libraries go into a folder that is not part of the code.
risks: Version ranges with a caret allow minor updates automatically, which can change behavior. No test command is listed, so changes are not checked automatically.
debug: If install or build fails, check the Node.js version and whether a lock file exists. Try deleting the downloaded library folder and installing again. Compare the library versions with the error message.
